summary: Montenegro lets citizens of the EU, UK, US and around 60 other countries and territories visit visa-free for up to 90 days (30 days for Peru, and until 31 October 2026 for Russia, Belarus, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia), and travelers who do need a visa can instead enter for up to 30 days on a valid Schengen, US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visa or residence permit.

conditionalWaivers.text: Holders of a valid Schengen, US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visa, or of a residence permit from the Schengen area or one of those countries, may enter Montenegro without a visa and stay up to 30 days (never beyond the validity of the visa or permit). The visa does not need to be multiple-entry or already used. Holders of an APEC Business Travel Card get the same 30 days.

passportValidity.text: Montenegro's foreign ministry says a foreign travel document is valid for entry if it was issued within the last ten years and will not expire until at least three months after your planned departure from Montenegro. If you need a visa, the passport must be valid at least three months longer than the visa.

declarations.text: All foreign visitors must register with the local tourism office or the police within 24 hours of arrival. Hotels and some holiday lets must register you; if you stay in private accommodation, make sure the registration is done. Not registering can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises being wary of pickpockets in tourist hot spots, beaches, airports and on public transport and not leaving luggage in a parked vehicle. It says incidents of violent crime between organised criminal groups can affect others close by, and that hikers have got lost in the mountains after leaving marked paths.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors must register with the local tourism office or police within 24 hours of arrival, and that you may be fined, detained or face a court appearance if you do not. If you stay in private accommodation, the UK says to make sure you complete the registration yourself.
Montenegro uses the euro although it is not an EU member: the European Central Bank lists it among the countries that use the euro without a formal arrangement.

If your nationality needs a visa but you hold a valid Schengen, US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visa or residence permit, you can enter Montenegro visa-free for up to 30 days.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Montenegro?
faq.answer: Most visitors don't: citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and around 60 other countries and territories can stay up to 90 days visa-free, and Peruvians 30 days. Russians, Belarusians, Turks and Saudis get 30 days until 31 October 2026 and need a visa from 1 November 2026. Nationalities that do need a visa can either apply at a Montenegrin embassy or enter on a valid Schengen, US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visa or residence permit for up to 30 days.

faq.question: Can I enter Montenegro with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes — holders of a valid Schengen visa or a Schengen-country residence permit (and equally US, UK, Irish, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand or Japanese visas and permits) may enter and stay up to 30 days without a Montenegrin visa, as long as the document remains valid. The visa does not need to be multiple-entry or already used.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Montenegro?
faq.answer: US passport holders can stay up to 90 days without a visa, under Montenegro's Decree on Visa Regime.

faq.question: Does Montenegro use the euro?
faq.answer: Yes. The European Central Bank lists Montenegro among the countries that use the euro without a formal arrangement with the EU; Montenegro is not an EU member.

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Montenegro?
faq.answer: Not until 31 October 2026: Montenegro's Decree on Visa Regime lets Russian citizens enter visa-free for up to 30 days until then. After that date the exemption lapses and a visa is required.

faq.question: Can EU citizens enter Montenegro with just an ID card?
faq.answer: Yes — EU citizens can enter with a national ID card for short stays of up to 30 days, and citizens of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Serbia can use their ID card for up to 90 days under the Western Balkans freedom-of-movement agreement. With a passport, EU citizens can stay up to 90 days.
